system.summary: Lee-Worcester sign cipher (1526-29): graphic-sign alphabet with word and name signs.
system.sibling_key: Tomokiyo's Lee-Worcester key, document on DECODE R8566
system.notes: Cipher only in four short runs of R8566. The other DECODE records (R8458-R8460, R8462, R8536-R8538, R8542-R8544, R8549, R8550, R8561, R8585-R8587, and R8602 of 20 Apr 1529 R8578 of 16 Oct 1528 and R8547-R8548 of 29 June 1527, all added later) are clear despatches with no cipher, so they are not listed as documents.

prior_solution.where: Interlinear contemporary decipherment in R8566; Tomokiyo key on DECODE R8566

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.

solution.what: Downloaded all 46 images of the 17 DECODE records and the key document on R8566 with the session cookie.
Looked at every page: 16 records are clear despatches to Wolsey with no cipher; R8566 has four short cipher runs.
Transcribed the contemporary interlinear decipherment of the four runs in R8566.
Spot-checked against Tomokiyo's Lee-Worcester key: signs under 'possibilite ... good' read p-o-ss-i-b-i-l-i-t-e and g-o-o-d.
Downloaded the two images of DECODE R8602 (catalogue 104, Cotton Vesp. C IV f. 341, 20 Apr 1529) with the session cookie.
Looked at both pages: a clear English despatch of Lee to Wolsey dated at Saragossa 20 April 1529, with postscript and signature; no cipher.
Catalogue 106 (DECODE R8578, Vesp. C IV f. 284, 16 Oct 1528, 'Epus Wigorn, Ed. Lee'): downloaded both images with the session cookie.
Looked at both pages of R8578: a clear English despatch of Ghinucci and Lee to Wolsey, Valladolid 16 Oct 1528, on English ships seized by the Emperor's subjects; no cipher sign on either page.
Read the full clear text of R8578 (both pages) into r8578_reading.txt.
Downloaded the two images of DECODE R8582 (catalogue 105, Vesp. C IV f. 300/old 276, 18 Nov 1528).
Applied Tomokiyo's Lee-Worcester key to R8582: 'worde for worde', 'erle of Desmonte' read; a full cipher page, no interlinear decipherment.
Letters and Papers IV no. 4948 calendars R8582 as cipher with 'Decipher of the above by Tuke' at f. 276*; summary agrees (earl of Desmond's courier).
Downloaded the two images of DECODE R8465 (catalogue 102) and its key document with the session cookie.
Transcribed the three cipher lines on f. 238v sign by sign.
Applied Tomokiyo's Lee-Worcester key (DOC_8465): 'thynke yf your grace speke somme thynge herof to the Emperoris ambassador ... come I thynke they wolde be gladde to see your grace contente'.
Letters and Papers iv no. 2097 (BHO) prints the same passage deciphered in italics; the reading agrees.
Catalogue 116 (DECODE R8547-R8548, Vesp. C IV ff. 139-140, 29 June 1527, 'Ed. Lee Almosinar'): downloaded all four images with the session cookie.
Looked at all four pages: one clear English despatch of Lee to Wolsey, Valladolid 29 June 1527 ('your grace most bounden priest'), split across the two records; no cipher sign on any page.
Catalogue 109 (DECODE R8552-R8555, R8568, R8573, Vesp. C IV, 1527, 'Eps. Wigorn'): downloaded all 18 images with the session cookie; contact sheet.
R8552-R8555 are clear leaves of L&P IV 3271 (17 July 1527); R8568 has its cipher runs deciphered interlinearly.

R8573 (Burgos, MS dated 26 Dec 1527) is a real cipher letter with no gloss; matched to L&P IV 3518 through its ciphered postscript's clear gloss ('not yet spoken of the French king's cession of the title of Milan'); L&P records Tuke's 5-page decipherment and misdates the letter 26 Oct.
Downloaded the two images of DECODE R8559 (catalogue 112, Vesp. C IV f. 164/old 152, July 1527) and Tomokiyo's key document on the record.

Applied Tomokiyo's Lee-Worcester key to the one cipher run on p. 2 of R8559: the '-mation' letters fit the interlinear gloss 'but the intimation'; rest of both pages clear English, p. 1 signs are reference marks.
Downloaded the eight images of DECODE R8575 (catalogue 107, Vesp. C IV ff. 262-265/old 243-244, 28 July 1528).

Letters and Papers IV no. 4564 calendars R8575 as 'Mostly cipher, pp. 7' with '2. Decipher by Tuke. Pp. 7' at f. 245; the clear passages on p. 1 (Radcliff, the ship taken in Bayonna in Galicia) match the summary word for word.
Catalogue 101: downloaded the 13 images of R8472, R8473, R8533, R8535 and Tomokiyo's key documents with the session cookie.
R8472 and R8535 clear; R8473 f. 245 and R8533 ff. 109-110 carry the Lee-Worcester sign cipher.
L&P iv 2173 (13 May 1526, deciphered by Tuke), 3055 (20 Apr 1527 duplicate of 3028, 8 Apr, Tuke's decipher at R.O.).
R8473 read sign by sign with Tomokiyo's key; then found Tuke's decipherment is image 4 of the record; agrees word for word.
R8533 first pass with Tomokiyo's key: about 83% (estimated).
Used L&P iv 3028's quotations of the 8 April original as a crib for R8533: 85.7% then 86.4% counted.
Third pass: ÷ with bar = them, Ⱶ = the Emperor, # = would, the 'marquis' group = INACHUS; 414/457 (90.6%). Name signs and underlined clusters stay open.
Catalogue 114 (DECODE R8556, Vesp. C IV f. 161, 1527, 'Bpp. Worecestr, Ed. Lee Eleem.'): downloaded both images with the session cookie.
Looked at both pages: a clear English leaf (old f. 149) of the 17 July 1527 despatch to Wolsey (L&P IV 3271), following R8552-R8555; no cipher sign.
Catalogue 113 (R8557, Vesp. C IV f. 162): both images downloaded and viewed; clear English secretary hand, no cipher signs.
Catalogue 108 (DECODE R8574, Vesp. C IV ff. 259-261, 1528, 'B. Worc., Ed. Lee'): downloaded all six images with the session cookie.

Looked at all six pages: a clear English letter headed 'Hispania 1528', signed 'Hier. Eps Wigornien / Edouarde Lee', advising a 'right honourable' correspondent (not Wolsey, who is named in the third person) how to answer the Emperor on the particular peace and the pledges; no cipher sign on any page.

Catalogue 115 (R8551, Vesp. C IV f. 156): both images viewed at full resolution; Lee's own clear English hand, Valladolid 5 June 1527, no cipher sign (a struck-through passage is ordinary script); matched to L&P IV 3152 by the christening of Prince Philip.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): sign-by-sign readings r8473_reading.txt and r8533_reading.txt (transcription and decryption in one file); R8465 signs copied from NOTES.md to texts/R8465_transcription.txt; R8566's contemporary interlinear decipherment plaintext.txt (its cipher signs were never transcribed); key additions to Tomokiyo's table copied from NOTES.md and r8473_reading.txt to texts/key.md

Reading audit, per-document pass (George Lasry's sentence test): R8566, R8465 and R8473 read; r8533_reading.txt is a worksheet with holes in several sentences and f. 109r not re-read (C confirmed). R8533 relabelled decoded, not read; fraction_read 1 -> 0.445; class already solved kept.

Re-read (REREAD_BRIEF, b29): DECODE R8533 fetched (four images and DOC_8533, which is Tomokiyo's key table, not a decipherment). f. 109r, f. 109v and f. 110r read line by line on half-width three-line strips at full resolution; clear text transcribed as running text for the first time; cipher runs re-checked sign by sign against the pass-2 worksheet, 12 corrections (R8533_corrections.tsv).

Running reading R8533_reading.md and English R8533_en.md. Score: 0.158 clean sentences with the modern word list, 0.895 (85/95) explicit holes only; the sentences hold. State decoded, not read -> read (grade B); fraction_read 0.445 -> 1.0.
Read bar applied per document (v10): 2 of 4 documents marked read measure under 95% of words read as sense (v2_score explicit holes) and are now read in part; read_share recorded for each.

Full-texts audit (section I): tried to reach the cipher of R8566 for a transcription. Nothing in the folder under another name; DECODE public API and record page: no transcription or attachment; full-size images return the 'Insufficient permissions to see the full image' placeholder without a login (thumbnails only); the British Library digitised-manuscripts page shows no online copy of Vespasian C IV. Recorded transcription_missing; nothing transcribed.

outcome.method_basis: Tomokiyo's Lee-Worcester key, attached to DECODE R8566, read the cipher runs of R8566, R8582, R8472-73 and R8533 (the last 90.6% with L&P IV 3028 as crib); every run had also been deciphered at the time (interlinear on R8566, Tuke's decipherments calendared in L&P IV).
outcome.notes: Read at the time; 16 of 17 records carry no cipher. Nothing new to read. R8602 (catalogue 104, 1529) is the same: clear, no cipher. R8578 (catalogue 106, 16 Oct 1528) is the same: clear, no cipher. R8582 (catalogue 105, 18 Nov 1528) is a full cipher page, read at the time by Tuke (L&P IV 4948 ii). R8559 (catalogue 112, July 1527) is clear with one short cipher run deciphered interlinearly ('but the intimation'); part of L&P IV 3271. Catalogue 101: R8472-73 (13 May 1526, to Henry VIII) read at the time by Tuke (image 4), re-read, agrees; R8535 clear; R8533 (20 Apr 1527 duplicate) read at the time from the original (Tuke, TNA), re-read here 90.6% with the L&P crib. R8557 (catalogue 113, 1527) is clear, no cipher. R8574 (catalogue 108, 1528) is clear, no cipher. R8551 (catalogue 115, 'Edouard Lee Almosinar', Valladolid 5 June 1527, L&P IV 3152) is clear, no cipher. 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: R8533 decoded, not read; fraction_read 1 -> 0.445. Class already solved kept: every run was deciphered at the time (L&P IV).

Without a login DECODE serves only 200-px thumbnails of this record (on 14 Nov 2026 a full-size request returned the placeholder image 'Insufficient permissions to see the full image'), and its record page and public API carry no transcription; the British Library's digitised-manuscripts page showed no online copy of Cotton MS Vespasian C IV. texts.label: R8566, Vesp. C IV ff. 170-173, Valladolid, 17 July 1527 (contemporary interlinear decipherment)
texts.summary: Joint despatch of Edward Lee and Girolamo Ghinucci to Wolsey; four short cipher runs, each deciphered above the line at the time. Among them, Lee and Ghinucci propose the daughter of Portugal for the Duke of Richmond (Henry Fitzroy) and discuss giving the duchy of Milan back to Francesco Sforza.

texts.label: R8465, Vesp. C III f. 238v, Seville, 15 April 1526
texts.summary: Lee to Wolsey, holograph: three cipher lines advising that if Wolsey speaks of the matter to the Emperor's ambassador who is coming, they will be glad to see him content. Letters and Papers Henry VIII iv no. 2097 already prints the passage.

texts.label: R8473, Vesp. C III f. 245, Seville, 13 May 1526
texts.summary: Lee to Henry VIII: two cipher blocks, read sign by sign with Tomokiyo's key and checked against Tuke's contemporary decipherment (the record's image 4). The Imperial court waits on events in France; the Spaniards about Milan; the French King sends men-of-arms and foot into Burgundy; Hesdin not to be delivered; Moncada's commission after suppressing the Moors of Valencia (L&P IV 2173).
texts.note: 24 Oct 2026: 92.1% of the words of r8473_reading.txt read as sense (v2_score explicit holes); coherent sentences but under the 95% read bar, so read in part.

texts.label: R8533, Vesp. C IV ff. 109-110, Valladolid, 20 April 1527 (running reading, re-read 23 Oct 2026)
texts.summary: Lee to Wolsey, a duplicate of his letter of 8 April (L&P IV 3028, used as crib, lp3028.txt): Almain's warning not to trust the French King, Perot's letter on the King of England's offer of his daughter and Boulogne, the Duke of Richmond 'whome they intend to make kynge of Irelande', the French King hated in France, and wives for Richmond (the daughter of the queen of Portugal, the daughters of Denmark).

reading_review.note: Read 23 Oct 2026 (b29): all three written pages re-read line by line on the full-size DECODE images (P1, P4, P2), the clear text transcribed as running text for the first time and the cipher runs re-checked sign by sign with Tomokiyo's key (12 worksheet corrections, R8533_corrections.tsv); Tuke's interlinear on f. 110r agrees. Body 0.158 clean sentences with the modern word list (1527 spelling), 0.895 (85/95) counting explicit holes; the sentences hold; holes are name codes, underlined clusters, blots and a few clear words. 2 letters and 1 code sign rest on a look-alike reading (Perot/Perote; the King's cross).

texts.note: 24 Oct 2026: 93.8% of the words of R8533_reading.md read as sense (v2_score explicit holes); coherent sentences but under the 95% read bar, so read in part.
